Information since May remains constructive: a strong labor market, moderate growth, below-2-percent inflation, and an on-hold policy rate with a mild easing bias (one dissent favoring a cut). The Financial Stability Report lens tempers this view: it notes that economic fundamentals influence market liquidity and valuations, and that economic activity affects corporate borrowers’ investment and employment—relevant given soft business fixed investment. It also flags pockets of vulnerability in credit (credit standards and leveraged loans; rising balances among near-prime/subprime borrowers), and market signals (declining 10-year Treasury yields relative to cap rates, and softer investor appetite for corporate bonds) that could amplify downside risks even in an otherwise stable backdrop. Netting these, the outlook is still positive but more two-sided than the initial take, warranting a cautious stance.
